summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and prior right knee replacement was admitted with worsening right knee pain, fever, and hypotension. She was found to have septic arthritis of the prosthetic knee, leading to septic shock and acute kidney injury. She underwent surgical removal of the infected prosthesis and placement of a temporary spacer. IV antibiotics were started and continued for six weeks. Her kidney function returned to baseline, and she improved clinically. She was discharged to an extended care facility for inpatient physical therapy and IV antibiotic administration, with plans for hardware revision in six weeks.
